headline: The week opens with the Nasdaq 100 at a record after Friday's 29,000 September payrolls print cut bets on another Fed hike, while India heads into Wednesday's RBI decision on an eighth straight weekly Nifty loss, the longest losing run since 2001.

summary.us: September payrolls came in at 29,000 against estimates clustered around 88,000 to 90,000 with unemployment at 4.2 percent, and traders cut bets on further Fed tightening. The Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.19 percent at 27,190.86 with the Nasdaq 100 at a record, the S and P 500 rose 0.74 percent to 7,722.85 and the Dow added 0.49 percent to 51,182.11, while the 10 year Treasury yield still finished higher at about 5.28 percent.
summary.india: Indian markets were shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti, so Thursday's close stands: the Nifty 50 fell 0.88 percent to 22,421.95 and Bank Nifty 0.33 percent to 54,450.75, an eighth consecutive weekly decline that coverage calls the longest since 2001, on foreign selling, crude near 91 dollars and rate increase fears. Foreign investors sold about 9,484 crore rupees of cash equities on 1 October while domestic institutions bought about 10,042 crore, and the rupee sits near 96.30 with the RBI decision due Wednesday.
summary.global: Hong Kong had Asia's worst session on Friday, the Hang Seng down 2.60 percent to 23,972.29 as HSBC, Alibaba and Tencent fell on the move in US yields, while the Nikkei lost 0.94 percent to 68,309.46; Europe rebounded, the DAX up 1.17 percent to 25,231.20 and the FTSE 100 up 0.32 percent to 10,462. Brazil votes in the first round today after the Ibovespa jumped 2.63 percent to 192,115 on Friday, and the G7 agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel as Strait of Hormuz constraints kept WTI near 91 dollars.

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms for four days and then handed them back on Friday. The US 10 year Treasury yield touched about 5.23 percent intraday midweek, described in coverage as the highest since June 2007, which pushed the dollar index to fresh 2026 highs, sent gold about 3.5 percent lower on the week and left the Dow down 1.3 percent and the S and P 500 down 0.3 percent even after Friday's bounce. Friday's September payrolls print of 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.2 percent, cut October Fed hike pricing to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent with Nvidia at an intraday record and Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries. India had the worse week and the shorter one: the Nifty fell 2.78 percent to 22,421.95 by Thursday's close, within 0.4 percent of its 52 week low, on rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and foreign selling of about 44,000 crore rupees in September, before markets shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti. Hong Kong reopened from its own holiday to its largest fall since March with HSBC down 5.7 percent, Tokyo slipped as September core CPI came in at 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, and silver lost 5.5 percent while copper held near records on tight supply. Next week turns on the 7 October FOMC minutes and the Reserve Bank decision the same day, with TCS opening India's earnings season on 8 October and the Strait of Hormuz still the swing factor for oil.
